paragraphs: A minister serving a great king fell out of favour. As punishment, the king had him locked at the top of a very tall tower and left there to die.

But the minister had a loyal wife. She came to the foot of the tower at night and called up, asking how she could help him. He told her to come back the next night with a long rope, some strong twine, pack thread, silken thread, a beetle and a little honey.

Puzzled, she did as he asked. Following his instructions, she tied the silken thread securely to the beetle, dabbed a drop of honey on its horns and set it on the tower wall, facing upwards. Off it went. Smelling the honey just ahead of it, the beetle crawled slowly up and up, hoping to reach it, until at last it arrived at the top. The minister caught it and took hold of the silken thread.

He called down for his wife to tie the pack thread to the other end, and pulled it up. Then he did the same with the strong twine, and finally with the rope. After that, it was easy: he climbed down the rope and escaped.

Swamiji used this story to explain yoga. In our bodies, the movement of the breath is the silken thread. By taking hold of it and learning to control it, we gain hold of the pack thread of the nerve currents. From there we reach the strong twine of our thoughts, and finally the rope of prana, the vital energy. Mastering that, we reach freedom.
learn: Big breakthroughs usually start with something tiny and manageable, like a single thread. If your mind feels out of control, start with your breath. Small, patient steps can lead you out of the tallest tower.
